# OASIS conformance requirements checklist: Explicit Opaque Object cryptographic context for Register

**Purpose**: Review whether the Opaque Object context requirements are complete, clear, consistent, measurable, and fully bounded.
**Created**: 2026-10-13
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Scope and normative clarity

- [x] CHK001 Does the specification preserve §2.3's MAY as an explicit caller choice while keeping generic Opaque Object handling as the default? [Clarity]
- [x] CHK002 Does the specification explain why §2.3 makes Table 293 applicable only when Managed Cryptographic Object context is selected, despite generic Opaque Object exemptions in §§4.13, 4.15, and 4.17? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK003 Does the requirement ledger distinguish Register §6.1.43/Table 291 payload requirements from Table 293 conditional attributes? [Completeness]
- [x] CHK004 Does the specification correctly identify the Table 4 child rows Opaque Data Type and Opaque Data Value as REQUIRED, without incorrectly calling the parent row required? [Traceability]

## Scenario and edge-case coverage

- [x] CHK005 Are generic and cryptographic Opaque Object Register paths independently testable? [Coverage]
- [x] CHK006 Are all applicable Table 293 attributes, paired Algorithm/Length behavior, Key Block omission boundary, and Certificate-only exclusions stated? [Completeness]
- [x] CHK007 Does the specification prohibit inferring a Key Block from Opaque Data Value or parsing opaque payload bytes? [Security]
- [x] CHK008 Does it require exact caller-attribute preservation and unknown Opaque Data Type value preservation? [Compatibility]
- [x] CHK009 Are missing and mistyped Table 4 fields, missing crypto attributes, partial Algorithm/Length pairs, and non-Opaque context misuse explicitly covered? [Edge Case]
- [x] CHK010 Are local invalid requests tied to zero transport writes and NotSent delivery evidence? [Measurability]

## Wire, API, and evidence boundaries

- [x] CHK011 Does the contract keep context metadata out of the KMIP wire payload and leave server acceptance authoritative? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK012 Does the specification distinguish this attribute-context feature from later Cryptographic Usage Mask authorization? [Scope]
- [x] CHK013 Are cross-language parity and the accepted public API manifest dependency clear without claiming generated artifacts already exist? [Dependency]
- [x] CHK014 Does the documentation avoid claiming formal conformance, certification, or official test-case passes without evidence? [Compliance]
- [x] CHK015 Are catalog ownership, source locators, implementation references, tests, and generated traceability outputs included in the same implementation change? [Traceability]

- [x] CHK016 Does the Register contract require the Opaque Object item tag and Structure value when Object Type is Opaque Object? [Clarity]

## Notes

- Review the requirements and source mapping, not implementation behavior.
- A read-only independent review on 2026-10-13 marked CHK001–CHK016 satisfied against the pinned KMIP 2.1 source and project hierarchy. The reviewer found no blocking discrepancy; see the review evidence in the implementation session.
- Record any unresolved source discrepancy without editing pinned upstream files.
